findings.first_evidence: src/session/controller.ts:141:       const worksheet = options.worksheet ?? (options.template ? undefined : (options.workflow ?? this.workflow)?.source.worksheet);
findings.suggested_fix: Distinguish a fresh manual replacement from an activated saved workflow. Use options.worksheet for an explicit choice, options.workflow?.source.worksheet for explicit workflow reuse, and this.workflow?.source.worksheet only when no source run is active (the activated-workflow case). Leave worksheet undefined for a manual replacement so a multi-sheet workbook prompts for selection. Verify same-name and missing-name replacement cases.
findings.title: Fresh workbooks silently reuse the previous worksheet
findings.why_it_matters: After a user selects a sheet and configures a run, uploading another multi-sheet workbook inherits the old worksheet name. If the name exists, the new workbook is imported without a choice and may produce results from the wrong sheet. If it does not exist, the import fails without offering the available sheets. This is a silent wrong-result or missing-result path for replacement uploads.
findings.validation_reason: After an Excel run is configured with its selected sheet, the ordinary source-upload caller at Workspace.tsx:280 supplies no options, so controller.ts:141 reuses this.workflow.source.worksheet and parseXlsx at xlsx.ts:56–58 bypasses discovery or rejects the replacement if that name is absent, contrary to excel-fidelity.md:70; incidence was not measured.

findings.title: Worksheet choice leaks into the next workbook
findings.why_it_matters: After choosing a source worksheet, a later multi-sheet destination template can open with that same sheet name already selected. If the user proceeds without making a fresh template choice, headers come from the coincidentally named sheet in the template. This defeats the template's independent worksheet choice and can replace the output mapping with unintended headers.
findings.validation_reason: When a source and subsequent template share a sheet name, Workspace.tsx:38,318–324 retains the selected name after successful import and its template caller at :423–425 never clears it, enabling immediate import of the coincidentally named template sheet despite the independent-selection requirement at excel-fidelity.md:70; incidence was not measured.

findings.title: Test failure after selecting a worksheet
findings.why_it_matters: The new worksheet chooser requires a second import. If that import fails because the selected sheet cannot be parsed or has invalid headers, the prior committed run must remain usable. The session test ends at chooser cancellation, and the browser rejection test fails during initial discovery, so neither detects a regression in the second import's failure transition.
findings.validation_reason: For a second import that fails after worksheet selection, controller.ts:176–179 creates a distinct transition required by the plan's U9 failed-replacement scenario, but session.test.ts:178–192 exercises only discovery and cancellation and excel-input.spec.ts:199–208 explicitly exercises failures before any chooser, leaving that reachable failure transition and retained export unverified.

findings.title: Separate worksheet and delimiter status branches
findings.why_it_matters: The new worksheet arm is nested inside a CSV delimiter expression, so an Excel import announces a worksheet as a detected delimiter. The packed conditional also makes later source-specific status changes easy to apply to only one fragment of the sentence.
findings.validation_reason: Any successful Excel import supplies view.worksheet through processing.worker.ts:38, making Workspace.tsx:335 render 'worksheet <name> delimiter detected' because the delimiter suffix follows both branches; the existing Excel import callers reach this path.
